ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: After filling a cylindrical oil tank with a diameter of 52 cm with some oil, the cross-section is shown in the figure. If the maximum depth CD of the oil is 16 cm, calculate the width AB of the oil surface.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the problem statement, we have: $OC \perp AB$ at point D,\\
According to the perpendicular diameter theorem, point D is the midpoint of AB, $AB = 2BD$,\\
$\because$ the diameter is $52\,\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore$OB = $26\,\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore$OD = OC - CD = $26 - 16 = 10\,\text{cm}$,\\
By the Pythagorean theorem,\\
$BD = \sqrt{BO^2 - OD^2} = 24\,\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore$AB = \boxed{48}\,\text{cm}.
